name: White Chocolate Caramel Protein Cookies
description: White chocolate salted-caramel cookies on the High-Protein Sugar Cookie base (4 cookies; rebuilt here from the browned-butter lineage for a cleaner vanilla canvas and leaner macros - the browned-butter arm was deleted). White chocolate baking chunks (15 g: folded in late, a few pieces pressed on top to toast golden) + the excellent-rated real brown-sugar caramel sub-recipe (0.5 batch, cooked to saucy/pourable, flaky salt finish) carrying the entire caramel axis - no toffee unless the caramel reads weak after a bake (+53 cal lever, noted). Also the FIRST xanthan-in-a-cookie test: 1/8 tsp whisked into the dry against this base's tender-crumbly weakness. Batch 571 cal | 42.4P | 58.1C | 17.5F (fat ~27% of cals); ~143 cal | 10.6P per cookie, ratio ~13.5. To-make.

payload.instructionText: Whisk the dry base — AP flour, whey protein, SF pudding mix, Splenda, baking powder, salt, and the xanthan gum — until there are no protein clumps. The xanthan MUST go in here with the dry; straight into the wet it pearls into slime beads.

Stir to combine, folding in the white chocolate chunks in the last strokes (reserve a few pieces for the tops), then stop and let the bowl sit untouched 5 minutes so the whey and pudding starches swell into a shapeable dough (if still tacky, chill 5 more minutes). Then cover and chill the dough ~30 minutes in the fridge — same as the browned-butter cookies: a proper chill firms it for cleaner shaping and a thicker, chewier bake.

Preheat oven/air fryer to 330°F. Divide the chilled dough into 4 equal balls on parchment and press firmly with your palm or a glass to your target thickness — this dough sets in the shape you give it, it won't spread, so keep them on the thicker side for a chewy center rather than thin and dry. Press the reserved white chocolate pieces onto the tops — they'll toast golden in the oven.

Once the cookies are set and cooled, drizzle with the brown-sugar caramel — cook it only to the thin saucy/pourable stage so it threads off a spoon — then add a small pinch of flaky salt over each (salted caramel is what keeps white chocolate from reading one-note sweet). Chill briefly to set the drizzle.

payload.text: First xanthan test in a cookie: 1/8 tsp for the batch, whisked into the dry. This base's known weakness is tender-crumbly - exactly the failure xanthan fixes (bendy, cohesive, moist chew at zero calories). Escalation: gummy/slick -> drop it next round; bouncy -> that's the gum stacking with the whey's elasticity, xanthan comes out of cookies. A real chew win graduates it to the other cookie bases. Never exceed 1/4 tsp per batch.

White chocolate scorches faster than real chocolate, and the dough itself stays pale - the pressed-on chunks toasting golden is your only browning, and it's a butterscotch bonus. If the chunks are darkening past golden before the 8-min check, pull the tray; blackened white chocolate is bitter.

The cooked salted caramel carries the ENTIRE caramel axis - same component, same 0.5-batch amount as the excellent-rated Caramel + Graham cookies, so it's proven at this scale. If after a bake the caramel doesn't read strong enough against the white chocolate, the add-back lever is 10 g toffee bits folded in with the chunks (+53 cal and +3 g fat on the batch) - don't reach for it before tasting.
